risk: Stock received is not what was ordered or is never recorded, so the ledger and the warehouse diverge from the first transaction.
audit_objective: Confirm goods received are verified against the order and recorded promptly and accurately.
what_to_review: Verification of quantity, quality and specification at receipt
Timeliness of receipt posting against physical arrival
Put-away accuracy and location recording
Rejected and quarantined stock handling
Receipts without a purchase order
procedures: Observe receiving and test whether counts and inspections are genuinely performed or documents simply signed.
Compare receipt posting timestamps to carrier delivery times and quantify delays.
Test put-away accuracy by selecting system locations and verifying physical presence.
Test the disposition of rejected stock — returned, scrapped or quietly absorbed.
red_flags: Deliveries signed without counting
Receipts posted in batches days later
Stock in locations the system does not show
Rejected goods with no return evidence
plain: If what arrives is not properly checked and recorded, every stock figure after that point is already wrong.

risk: Stock is stolen or damaged in storage, and weak custody controls mean the loss only appears at the next count.
audit_objective: Assess physical custody controls over inventory and the segregation between custody and record-keeping.
what_to_review: Physical security — access control, CCTV, high-value cages
Segregation between warehouse custody and inventory record maintenance
Movement authorisation between locations
Handling of samples, promotional and staff purchases
Damage and write-off authorisation
procedures: Walk the warehouse and test physical access controls and segregation of high-value stock.
Test whether warehouse staff can amend inventory records to conceal a shortfall.
Test stock transfers between locations for authorisation and receipt confirmation at the destination.
Analyse write-offs by location, reason and approver for concentration.
red_flags: Warehouse staff with inventory adjustment rights
Transfers despatched but never received
Write-offs concentrated before a count
Access lists including former employees
evidence: System access rights for inventory adjustment
plain: Stock sitting in a warehouse is portable and saleable, which is why custody controls matter more than they look.

risk: Counts are performed by the people responsible for the stock, so discrepancies are corrected rather than reported.
audit_objective: Confirm counting is independent, covers the population and results in investigated, approved adjustments.
what_to_review: Count programme coverage, frequency and risk weighting
Independence of counters from custody
Recount and tolerance rules
Investigation of variances before adjustment
Approval authority for inventory adjustments
procedures: Attend a count unannounced and perform test counts in both directions.
Test coverage — identify items and locations never counted in the period.
Test whether variances above tolerance were investigated before the adjustment was posted, or simply posted.
Analyse adjustments by item, location and approver for offsetting positives and negatives.
red_flags: Counts performed by the storekeeper alone
Positive and negative adjustments offsetting to near zero
Items never selected for count
Adjustments posted before investigation
plain: Counting stock is how you find out what is really there. Letting the same people count their own stock defeats the point.

risk: Inventory is valued using costs that no longer reflect reality, so margin and stock value are both wrong.
audit_objective: Confirm inventory cost reflects actual purchase and conversion cost on a supportable basis.
what_to_review: Costing method and its consistent application
Standard cost roll frequency and approval
Overhead absorption basis and capacity assumptions
Purchase price variance analysis and disposition
Cost of items with volatile input prices
procedures: Recompute unit cost for a sample of items from purchase invoices and conversion cost data.
Test the overhead absorption rate against actual overhead and activity, including treatment of idle capacity.
Analyse purchase price variances by item and test whether they are investigated or simply absorbed.
Test the timing of the last standard cost roll against input price movements.
red_flags: Standards unchanged through a period of significant price inflation
Idle capacity absorbed into inventory value
Variances written off without analysis
Overhead absorbed on an outdated activity base
evidence: Purchase invoices and conversion cost data
plain: The cost attached to each item decides both the stock value and the reported margin on every sale.

subprocess: Obsolescence, Slow-Moving and Net Realisable Value
risk: Stock that will never sell at cost remains valued at cost, overstating assets and deferring a loss already incurred.
audit_objective: Confirm inventory is carried at the lower of cost and net realisable value.
what_to_review: Ageing and slow-moving reporting accuracy
Provisioning policy and its consistent application
Evidence of realisable value — recent sales, forecasts, market prices
Management overrides of the formula-driven provision
Treatment of discontinued lines and engineering changes
procedures: Test the ageing report logic — ageing based on receipt date can understate slow-moving items if stock is rotated in the system.
Compare carrying value to recent selling prices net of costs to sell for a sample of lines.
Test management overrides to the provision for support and approval.
Identify stock with no movement in twelve months and test the justification for holding it at cost.
red_flags: Provision released to support results
Ageing reset by internal transfers
Discontinued lines still held at full cost
Realisable value supported by optimistic forecasts
plain: Stock that will never sell at full price is worth less than the books say, and saying so is uncomfortable.

risk: Stock held by others or in transit is recorded on the wrong balance sheet, or lost entirely because nobody is counting it.
audit_objective: Confirm that inventory ownership and location are correctly reflected wherever the stock physically sits.
what_to_review: Identification of stock held at third parties and by agents
Consignment agreements and ownership terms
Confirmation and counting of externally held stock
Goods in transit and the shipping terms that determine ownership
Customer-owned stock held on the premises
procedures: Obtain confirmations from third parties holding stock and reconcile to the ledger.
Test consignment agreements to determine when ownership and risk transfer, and confirm accounting follows.
Test goods in transit at period end against shipping terms.
Identify customer-owned material on site and confirm it is excluded from inventory.
red_flags: Third-party stock never counted or confirmed
Consignment treated as sold on despatch
In-transit stock recorded by both parties or neither
Customer material indistinguishable from own stock
plain: Stock held elsewhere, or in transit, is easy to count twice or not at all.

risk: Scrap and returned goods are removed from the system without control, providing a route for stock to leave the business.
audit_objective: Confirm scrap and returns are authorised, evidenced and any residual value captured.
what_to_review: Scrap authorisation, witnessing and disposal evidence
Proceeds from scrap sales and where they are recorded
Customer returns receipt, inspection and disposition
Restocking accuracy and valuation of returned goods
Warranty and repair stock movements
procedures: Test scrap transactions for authorisation and independent witnessing of destruction or disposal.
Trace scrap sale proceeds to bank receipts and the ledger.
Test returned goods from receipt through inspection to restock, repair or scrap, and check valuation at each step.
Analyse return volumes by customer and product for patterns.
red_flags: Scrap disposed of without witness
Scrap sale proceeds received in cash
Returns restocked at full value without inspection
Return rates far above normal for one customer
evidence: Scrap sale invoices and bank receipts
plain: Scrap and returns are a legitimate-looking route for stock to leave the building.
